scope: Compare the current analytic-forcing regularity preprint with its cited OpenAI construction data; not an independent proof verification or physical conclusion.

regularity_preprint.title: Regularity of asymptotically axisymmetric solutions to the 3D Navier-Stokes equations with analytic forcing

crosswalk.openai_force_class: C-infinity compactly supported in space-time, stated in OpenAI Lemma 10.3; implies bounded spatial C2 norm through the endpoint.
crosswalk.force_endpoint_jets: OpenAI Lemma 10.2 states that every mixed derivative has an endpoint limit partial_x^alpha F_j(x) with partial_x^alpha F_j(0)=0 for every alpha,j. The Lemma 10.3 smooth extension therefore has zero full space-time Taylor jet at (0,1).
crosswalk.angular_mean_anisotropic_bounds: Preprint Appendix A.2 derives the bounds it uses from cited OpenAI source statements.
crosswalk.collapsing_exact_axisymmetric_core: Preprint Appendix A.3 derives a nonempty axisymmetric core at each preterminal time from cited OpenAI support geometry.
crosswalk.pure_swirl_open_set: Preprint Appendix A.3 derives an off-axis open space-time set E on which u_r=u_z=0.
crosswalk.axis_value: OpenAI Appendix B.1 sets U*(eta)=4 eta+j0, 0<j0<=0.05; the preprint derives u_z(0,-tau)=j0 tau^(-A) and partial_z u_z(0,-tau)=4/tau for small tau>0.

premises: uniform spatial C2 bound on force through endpoint
local-uniform spatial real analyticity of force on interior time cylinders
anisotropic Type-II estimates on angular mean through order two
nonempty exactly axisymmetric core at each preterminal time
conditional_results.contrapositive_for_openai_claim: If the cited source crosswalk holds and the OpenAI construction is singular, its force violates the local-uniform spatial analyticity condition.
conditional_results.additional_corollary: Under the same crosswalk and singularity assumption, the force is not identically zero on any space-time cylinder B(R') x (-delta',0) around the point.

premises: u_r=u_z=0 on nonempty open E off axis over a time interval
u_z on axis is nonzero at the interval endpoint
candidate force has a common spatial real-analyticity bound on a ball intersecting E over the interval
conditional_results.deduction: Interior analyticity makes u_z spatially analytic; vanishing on E and the identity theorem force u_z to vanish on the connected ball, contradicting continuity and the nonzero axis value.
conditional_results.consequence: No such common spatial analyticity bound exists; force cannot vanish identically on that ball-time slab because zero is analytic.

premises: conditional nonvanishing on every neighborhood cylinder from preprint Corollary 2.3 and Appendix A crosswalk
conditional_results.deduction: All space-time derivatives of the extended force vanish at the singular point, while under the stated singularity/crosswalk assumptions the force is not identically zero in any surrounding space-time cylinder.
conditional_results.flatness_bound: For every finite m, f(x,t)=o((|x|+|t-1|)^m); hence its supremum on B(r) x (1-r^2,1) is o(r^m).
does_not_imply: positive lower bound on force amplitude

limitations: The preprint authors explicitly state they do not claim to verify the correctness of the OpenAI construction; this audit records and checks the cited implication chain, not the complete source proof.
Non-identically-zero in every neighborhood cylinder gives no positive lower bound on amplitude, duration, location, or actuation cost; flatness is only an upper-order statement.
No molecular, constitutive-viscosity, numerical-solver, or engineering-safety implication follows.
No simulation was run and no upstream software defect is identified.
